title: feat: introduce init-wave-selector and values partitioning for air-gapped cluster installs
author: Priya Nambiar
release_notes: Adds cluster-aware init-wave selection and optional values partitioning for air-gapped/private installs. Backwards compatible; operators can opt into partitioned values mode. Includes schema updates, templating helpers, tests, and docs.
description:
Motivation: Private/on-prem installs in environments with restrictive networking and per-cluster policy constraints need a way to (1) control which init jobs run per-cluster and per-wave, and (2) provide smaller, partitioned values blobs to avoid pushing large monolithic values into air-gapped registries. This PR introduces an 'init-wave-selector' template and a values partitioning convention which together let operators scope init jobs and values by cluster-profile.

What this PR does (single-string body): - Adds charts/private/templates/init-wave-selector.yaml: a small template that evaluates .Values.initWaves and a new .Values.clusterProfile to compute which hook jobs should run in a given cluster and wave. The template is intentionally deterministic (no randomness) and supports explicit include/exclude patterns. - Introduces charts/private/values.partitioned.schema.json: JSON schema additions to validate partitioned values (fields: partitionId, base64BlobRef, clusterProfile). - Adds a lightweight helm helper library charts/private/templates/_helpers/partitioner.tpl that offers split/merge helpers and a templated reference format for partitioned secrets. - Moves init job manifests into charts/private/templates/init-jobs/ and adds per-wave templating (init-job-partitioned.yaml, init-job-legacy.yaml) so legacy single-values installs keep working. - New chart helper scripts/scripts/helm-values-partitioner.go (CLI utility) to generate partitioned values blobs for airgap packaging; included in repo for operators to use during image bundle generation. - Adds tests in tests/helm/ that validate: (a) non-partitioned installs render the same resources as before, (b) partitioned installs produce smaller values secret manifests and correctly reference base64 blobs, and (c) init-wave-selector chooses the expected jobs for simple include/exclude cases. - Documentation under docs/private/airgap-values-partitioning.md with examples and migration steps.

Checklist: - [x] Schema validation (values.partitioned.schema.json) - [x] Backwards-compatible templating (legacy path preserved) - [x] Tests for both modes - [x] Small helper CLI for operators - [x] Docs and migration guidance - [x] Security review for secret reference format

Migration notes: Operators not opting into values.partitioned will see no change. For air-gapped installs where operators prefer to store values blobs as separate secrets or file artifacts, run scripts/helm-values-partitioner.go to generate partitioned blobs and update your install bundle to include the referenced secret artifacts. The templating accepts both inline values and referenced blobs to ease rollout.

Operational considerations: - init-wave-selector is evaluated at render time; it does not add runtime controller dependencies. For customers who need dynamic runtime gating, we recommend using the existing tenant bootstrap operator and keeping init-job templates unchanged. - Partitioned values are validated by the schema and the helm helper will error if required partition metadata is missing.

Links: Linear ENG-2241 (init-wave refactor), docs PR: #link-to-docs (internal), support ticket SUP-874 for a customer request that motivated partitioning.
